newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends flat to firmer.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends flat to firmer.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures ended unchanged to slightly higher Tuesday, lifted by trade buying, floor sources said.
October sugar finished up 0.02 cent a lb, at 12.05 cents, after ranging between 12.07 and 11.96. March ended unchanged, at 11.73, while the back months closed 0.02 to 0.09 higher.
Dealers said today's session mirrored recent market activity, with trade buying noted at the dips and speculators continuing to roll out of the October contract ahead of its September 30 expiry.
October's open interest was still relatively high at 68,668 lots on Monday, but traders said it was likely to drop with the October options expiry on Friday.

Traders also expect the October contract to continue to hover near the 12.00-cent strike price ahead of the options expiry, with near 20,000 lots of October calls still in the money up to 12.00 cents.
The October/March switch, which was the focus of much of the day's activity, ended at 0.32 cent Tuesday, compared to 0.30 cent at the close on Monday.

On the charts, traders pegged October support at 11.80 cents, with resistance seen at 12.10-12.15 cents. Second-month March's support was put at 11.50 and resistance was pegged at 11.75, the life-of-contract high.

Traders brushed aside news that the executive director of the International Sugar Organisation (ISO), Peter Baron, said Tuesday at an Asia sugar conference in New Delhi that surplus world sugar supplies in 1996/97 could weigh on prices.
"It is really too early to assess the 1996/97 crops," one trader said. "We'll get a more specific number towards the end of 1996."
